guarantees.title: Exact subject custody
guarantees.claim: A checked result names the exact local bytes or rooted structure to which that result applies.
guarantees.scope: Canonical MIW JSON records, proof dossiers, candidate checks, and sealed archives produced by the declared local paths.
invalidated_by: Any change to subject bytes, canonicalization, referenced roots, or the validating implementation requires a fresh result.

guarantees.title: Evidence classes are not silently promoted
guarantees.claim: Requirements, proposed correspondences, examples, executions, source proofs, and physical-world assumptions retain distinct typed statuses.
guarantees.scope: The obligation ledger, Zucchini import/binding, workbench execution, and generated explanations.
invalidated_by: A code or schema change that merges evidence classes, upgrades a proposal without its required evidence, or omits an open assumption.

guarantees.title: Malformed or unbound inputs refuse
guarantees.claim: Declared validation paths return a typed refusal or failing status instead of inventing missing meaning, identity, or evidence.
guarantees.scope: Public CLI operations, contract validation, dossier checks, and bounded workbench lowering/execution.
invalidated_by: An uncovered public operation, permissive fallback, unverifiable reference, or swallowed validation failure.

guarantees.title: Plans and explanations grant no authority
guarantees.claim: MIW-created plans, diagnostics, explanations, and receipts cannot authorize production effects or approve their own semantics.
guarantees.scope: The local constitutional control plane and all self-contract explanation outputs.
invalidated_by: Any path that treats a locally generated record as approval, law, admission, deployment authority, or independent review.

guarantees.title: External effects require explicit admission
guarantees.claim: Every registered loopback, process, database, or compiler effect requires explicit opt-in or an external gate.
guarantees.scope: Operations classified in the closed operation registry and executed through declared adapters.
invalidated_by: An exposed effectful operation missing from the registry, classified as read-only, or executable without its declared admission.

guarantees.title: Proof, examples, and headless execution retain their boundary
guarantees.claim: A source proof, concrete example run, imported report, and headless semantic court are reported as different observations with explicit claim ceilings.
guarantees.scope: Restricted scalar proof, BDD examples, Zucchini reports, and the semantic HeadlessRunner.
invalidated_by: A report or UI/headless result is represented as a mathematical proof, or an example result is represented as exhaustive.

guarantees.title: Qualification is zero-skip and source-stable
guarantees.claim: The qualification runner fails unless its distinct tests pass with zero errors, failures, and skips, required verifier coverage is present, and source bytes remain unchanged during the run.
guarantees.scope: The builder-authored local qualification runner on the exact host and source root named by its receipt.
invalidated_by: Any skipped, failed, or errored test; missing required verifier coverage; failing mutation; or a source-root change during qualification.

guarantees.title: The workbench exposes its own bounded contract
guarantees.claim: Every declared public guarantee resolves to enforcement paths, courts, tests, evidence schemas, invalidation conditions, nonclaims, and trusted assumptions in one sealed contract.
guarantees.scope: The checked SELF-CONTRACT.json and the self-contract-check and explain commands in this exact candidate.
invalidated_by: A changed contract root, orphaned nonclaim or assumption, missing enforcement path, uncovered court, undeclared explain operation, or failed self-explication court.

nonclaims.statement: MIW does not prove that a human-authored requirement is the right requirement.
nonclaims.reason: Formal or executable checks preserve the supplied meaning boundary; they cannot manufacture stakeholder intent.

nonclaims.statement: MIW does not prove arbitrary C++ or an arbitrary Zucchini codebase correct.
nonclaims.reason: Its native proof language and accepted integration lanes are deliberately bounded.

nonclaims.statement: MIW does not prove that database inventory equals physical inventory in a warehouse.
nonclaims.reason: Sensors, counting, fraud, loss, and operational reconciliation remain outside the mathematical model.

nonclaims.statement: MIW cannot guarantee an invariant while uncontrolled write paths bypass the governed operation.
nonclaims.reason: The system boundary must include every writer that can affect the protected state.

nonclaims.statement: No MIW receipt, plan, diagnostic, or explanation grants production authority.
nonclaims.reason: Operational authority belongs to an external institution and admission process.

nonclaims.statement: Builder-authored courts and tests are not independent review or certification.
nonclaims.reason: Independence requires a separately authorized reviewer and evidence process.

nonclaims.statement: Headless and mocked process tests do not prove native Windows appearance or the absence of visible console flash.
nonclaims.reason: That observation requires a real native UI acceptance lane.

nonclaims.statement: The self-contract does not recursively prove MIW or eliminate its trusted base.
nonclaims.reason: The checker, runtime, host, canonicalizer, proof translator/checker, and human semantic review remain relied upon.

nonclaims.statement: Equal hashes establish byte identity, not semantic correctness; unequal hashes do not by themselves establish semantic difference.
nonclaims.reason: Cryptographic identity and program meaning are separate claims.

nonclaims.statement: Reference-model and fixture success do not establish live PostgreSQL behavior unless the explicit live lane ran.
nonclaims.reason: Driver, server, transaction, retry, and deployment behavior require their own acceptance evidence.

trusted_assumptions.statement: The identified Python interpreter executes the checked MIW code according to its documented semantics.
trusted_assumptions.failure_effect: All Python-produced validations and receipts may be unsound.
trusted_assumptions.control: Record interpreter identity, use isolated mode, and repeat qualification on named hosts.

trusted_assumptions.statement: The named operating system and filesystem return the bytes MIW reads and durably preserve accepted writes.
trusted_assumptions.failure_effect: Observed identity, atomic replacement, or process behavior may differ from the receipt.
trusted_assumptions.control: Use fresh directories, explicit paths, fsync where implemented, and cross-host replay.

trusted_assumptions.statement: The canonical JSON and SHA-256 implementation bind records as specified.
trusted_assumptions.failure_effect: Roots may not identify the intended record content.
trusted_assumptions.control: Keep canonicalization small, test it, and verify exported artifacts independently.

trusted_assumptions.statement: The restricted source translator and native proof checker correctly implement their declared logic.
trusted_assumptions.failure_effect: A checked source-proof result may not establish its stated bounded invariant.
trusted_assumptions.control: Mutation tests, certificate replay, source review, and independent checker review.

trusted_assumptions.statement: The archive hash and closed manifest are checked by a trustworthy external mechanism at the transfer boundary.
trusted_assumptions.failure_effect: The consumer may run bytes other than the qualified candidate.
trusted_assumptions.control: Publish an external SHA-256 receipt and verify before extraction and execution.

trusted_assumptions.statement: Authorized humans review business meaning, mappings, waivers, and institutional policy.
trusted_assumptions.failure_effect: A mechanically consistent system may faithfully enforce the wrong rule.
trusted_assumptions.control: Require named review, explicit proposals, and requalification after approved changes.

trusted_assumptions.statement: A privileged adversary does not replace code, inputs, or outputs between validation and use.
trusted_assumptions.failure_effect: Local custody and effect gates can be bypassed outside MIW's process boundary.
trusted_assumptions.control: Use protected deployment custody, least privilege, external monitoring, and independent artifact verification.

claim_ceiling: This is a sealed, executable map of MIW's declared local guarantees and boundaries. It is not recursive self-proof, external truth, independent certification, semantic approval, or production authority.
